title: Adjustments in Medishield Life Premiums Given Difficult Climate
what_it_is: Adjustments in Medishield Life Premiums Given Difficult Climate

sections.label: MediShield Life premium questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Health about MediShield Life premium increases, affordability for seniors, assistance schemes, actuarial reports, reserves, lifetime premiums, surplus or loss, flexibility and coverage guarantees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the basis for the increase in MediShield Life premiums; (b) how can the premiums be kept affordable especially for the seniors; and (c) what are the assistance schemes available to help seniors who are unable to afford the premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health whether the full actuarial report for the current MediShield Life scheme and the proposed MediShield Life scheme revisions, including actuarial assumptions used, can be made available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the actuarial formula for the required reserves in the MediShield Life Fund; (b) whether it is unusual by international standards for a health insurance scheme to increase its premiums by 35% in a single adjustment; and (c) what is the total premium paid by a Singaporean for MediShield Life in his lifetime assuming the premiums are compounded at 2.5% interest and 4% interest respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health in respect of the increase in premiums following the review of MediShield Life (a) what is the surplus or loss since introduction of MediShield Life in 2015; (b) whether the Ministry can introduce more flexibility so that premiums are paid based on choice of coverage and illnesses covered; and (c) how will the Government guarantee coverage of an elderly when they default on the premiums mid-way through medical treatment.

sections.label: Subsidised hospitalisation cash payments
sections.summary: About eight in 10 patients today need to pay $100 or less in cash for their subsidised hospitalisation bills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: About eight in 10 patients today need to pay $100 or less in cash for their subsidised hospitalisation bills.

sections.label: Claimants, payouts and hospitalisation bills
sections.summary: Claimants rose about 30% and annual payouts about 40% over four years, while average public hospitalisation bills rose about 6% a year between 2001 and 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The number of claimants has increased by about 30% and the annual payouts have increased by about 40% over the last four years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Between 2001 and 2019, the average hospitalisation bill size in public healthcare institutions has increased by about 6% a year on average, and this is affected by medical cost inflation, demographics and medical advancements over these years.

sections.label: Government share of premiums
sections.summary: About 35% of total premiums collected in 2019 were paid for by the Government through subsidies and support schemes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Taken together, about 35% of the total premiums collected were paid for by the Government through various subsidies and support schemes in 2019.

sections.label: COVID-19 premium subsidy
sections.summary: A COVID-19 subsidy for all Singapore citizens will pay the bulk of the first-year premium increase, keeping the net increase to no more than about 10%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Government has therefore provided a COVID-19 subsidy for all Singapore citizens in the next two years, which will pay for the bulk of the premium increase in the first year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Taken together with existing premium subsidies and support, the net increase for all Singapore Citizens will be no more than about 10% in the first year after the MediShield Life review is implemented.

sections.label: Premiums collected 2016 to 2019
sections.summary: Between 2016 and 2019, a total of S$7.5 billion in premiums were collected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Between 2016 and 2019, a total of S$7.5 billion in premiums were collected.

sections.label: Fund Incurred Loss Ratio
sections.summary: The Fund's Incurred Loss Ratio averaged 104% from 2016 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Incurred Loss Ratio or ILR of the Fund was an average of 104% over the period from 2016 to 2019.

sections.label: Hepatitis C treatment and premiums
sections.summary: New Hepatitis C treatment costing about $600,000 a pill shows why a single formula is hard and premiums need regular review.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Even medications, for example, Hepatitis C used to have not much treatment except for liver transplant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But today, there is drug on the market that one pop of a pill – it costs about $600,000 a pill, a dose of treatment – can potentially eradicate Hepatitis C.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, I think it will be very, very hard to have a single formula to have that level of clarity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But the actuaries that use some of these current data to project will make adjustments over time and this is why we need to review our premiums on a regular basis, yearly, if not, every couple years, to take into account new treatment on the horizon, new changes in clinical practice, new utilisation patterns, so that we can reflect the premiums accurately.

sections.label: Incentives for healthy habits
sections.summary: Vouchers or incentives such as $100 NTUC vouchers a year could be given to people who clock 10,000 steps a day and have good diabetic control.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: You can give vouchers, for example, or give some form of incentive for people who clock 10,000 steps a day, who have good diabetic control and sugar intake; you can give them some incentive like maybe $100 NTUC vouchers a year or something like that.

sections.label: Taiwan actuarial report release
sections.summary: Taiwan's National Health Insurance Administration is required by law to release an actuarial report every five years, with the latest on its website.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, Taiwan's National Health Insurance Administration is required by law to release an actuarial report every five years, and their latest report is available on their website.

sections.label: MediShield Life premium calculation
sections.summary: MediShield Life premiums are proposed and calculated by external actuaries independent of the Government, based on their data and assumptions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I think very few people are actuarial experts who can understand the nuancing and the very complicated calculations that goes behind the scenes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I would say that MediShield Life premiums are, first of all, proposed and calculated by external actuaries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: That means, they are independent of the Government, they are a set of actuarial consultants who craft up the series of premiums that they think, based on data and assumptions that they made, that would be fair for to charge to the policyholders.

sections.label: MediShield data and premiums
sections.summary: Key information is published on the MOH website, and the question asks whether data exists comparing MediShield premiums with other countries' schemes and affordability for lower income groups.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Nonetheless, the key information that is available are already published transparently on the MOH website and those who are interested can take reference from there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I suppose the most obvious reason is because if we offer this to the private sector, there will be no takers, given the terms where, amongst others, it covers seniors, those with pre-existing conditions and also at a premium that is affordable to the lower income groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, I wanted to ask the Senior Minister of State whether he has the data to give us a sense of how are the MediShield premiums compared to the levels of other countries with similarly-run national schemes; whether are we priced at the level that is affordable to our lower income groups?

sections.label: MediShield Life universal scheme
sections.summary: MediShield Life was conceived as a universal scheme so no Singaporean is left behind, using MediSave, MediFund and premium support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And the sad thing we always talk about in the doctors' tea room is that, sadly, the people who needs the insurance the most are the ones who cannot afford it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This is why MediShield Life was conceived to be a universal Scheme to make sure that no single Singaporean will be left behind, even the poorest and the lowest of income; through whatever means: MediSave contributions, through MediFund, through additional premium support.

sections.label: Voluntary scheme premiums higher
sections.summary: For a voluntary healthcare system, raw premiums after revision range from 34% to 143% higher than MediShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Even then, for a voluntary healthcare system, the premiums compared to the revised MediShield Life premiums coming on stream before subsidy add-ons – that means just the raw premiums after the revision – the premiums range from being 34% to 143% higher than our MediShield Life.

sections.label: MediShield Life premium amounts
sections.summary: Revised MediShield Life premiums before subsidy are S$145 yearly for ages one to 20 and S$2,055 for citizens over 90.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: At the lowest end, at the one to 20-year-old age range, our revised MediShield Life premium before subsidy is S$145 a year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: At the extreme end of the age range, at more than 90 years old, the MediShield Life premium for Singapore citizens more than 90 years old before any form of subsidies is S$2,055.

sections.label: Fund size and government share
sections.summary: About $7 billion is inside, of which 35% comes from the Government, more than the $800 million mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Today, there are already about $7 billion or so inside, of which 35% of it comes from the Government.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: That is way more than $800 million that he was talking about.

sections.label: No denial of coverage
sections.summary: Coverage is universal and for life, and no Singaporean will be denied coverage if unable to pay premiums.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: When we talk about stress, I think it is important to remember my emphasis that this is universal, this is for life and importantly, no Singaporean will be denied coverage if you cannot pay premiums.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We will find means to subsidise, to cover with MediFund or additional payment support if needed.
